defect.problem: The holding field is truncated at “been…” and omits the limits that make the proposition accurate.
defect.proposed_fix: Complete the holding to say that a defendant may waive the Sixth Amendment right to counsel during police-initiated interrogation after counsel has been requested or appointed, provided the waiver is voluntary, knowing, and intelligent and no Edwards/Miranda invocation bars questioning.

reasons: The opinion supports the core waiver proposition: it says the Sixth Amendment right may be waived if voluntary, knowing, and intelligent.
The opinion also says a defendant may waive the right whether or not already represented by counsel, and that Miranda warnings typically suffice.
But the content holding under review is incomplete and would overclaim if read without the voluntary/knowing/intelligent and Edwards limitations.
residual_risks: No disclosed official-pagination map was needed to verify support, but any page-pin assertion would need separate review.
reviewed.suggested_tightening: Avoid ellipsis in the holding field; state the full rule and the Edwards/Miranda caveat.

reasons: The opinion expressly concerns the scope and continued viability of Michigan v. Jackson’s Sixth Amendment counsel rule.

The opinion discusses Sixth Amendment waiver, police-initiated interrogation, appointment/request of counsel, and overrules Jackson, so placement under Sixth Amendment Right to Counsel as a key progeny/refinement case is supported.
residual_risks: The disclosed files do not define the home-role taxonomy, so review is limited to whether the role is substantively plausible from the opinion text.
